title: A balanced binary search tree and a tree reduced to a chain
summary: The same seven nodes satisfy the same search tree ordering, but the shape changes the length of a search path.
context: In a binary search tree, all values in a node’s left subtree are smaller than its value and all values in its right subtree are larger. Arrows point from parent to child.
description: The left figure is labeled “Balanced binary search tree.” Root 4 has left and right children 2 and 6; 2 has children 1 and 3, and 6 has children 5 and 7. Counting gives three levels and a height of 2 edges. The right figure, “Degenerate binary search tree,” starts at root 7 and follows only left children: 7 → 6 → 5 → 4 → 3 → 2 → 1. Every right link is empty. There are seven levels and a height of 6 edges.
result: In a balanced binary search tree, search, insertion, and deletion can take logarithmic time. In a single chain the worst case visits every node, taking O(n) time.

frames.title: A balanced binary search tree and a tree reduced to a chain
frames.explanation: Both trees contain the same values 1 through 7 and satisfy the strict binary search tree ordering. Searching for leaf 1 on the left visits just three nodes along 4 → 2 → 1. On the right it visits all seven along 7 → 6 → 5 → 4 → 3 → 2 → 1. The figure compares two structures without showing any insertions or deletions that would change one into the other.
